takeaway: One litre of normal saline contains 154 mmol of sodium. Three bags a day meet an NBM adult's fluid needs; daily sodium need is about 100 mmol.

question.text: A 24-year-old woman with appendicitis is nil by mouth on IV fluids. The first bag is 1 L of normal saline. How much sodium is in this bag?

lines.text: She is nil by mouth, so all her fluid comes through the drip.
The average adult needs about three litres of fluid a day.
That is easily met with three bags of intravenous fluid, each run over eight hours.
Now look at the first bag: one litre of normal saline.
Normal saline is salt water, so it carries sodium.
One litre contains one hundred and fifty-four millimoles of sodium.
An adult needs about a hundred millimoles of sodium per day, so this bag supplies plenty.
